items.title: 61520_Teddy Edwards oral history interview
items.q: Paul Bascomb was the tenor player's name, when he first came out of prison.

ctx.x: All the bands! They had everything on the jukebox. You know, Roy Eldridge with Gene Krupa and, you know, "After You've Gone"...

Paul Bascomb was the tenor player's name, when he first came out of prison... This band was From Alabama State, Erskine Hawkins' band, the 'Bama State Collegians.. And they had several bands. Milton Trenier also came out of that. He had a 'Bama State band out of the same college. But Erskine Hawkins was really flying high, you know, and he was some trumpet player. But he had some other guys that could play, too, and he let them play, you know. And Julian Dash was a fine tenor player. And this alto player, I think…

Well, I heard all these people, you know. I used to listen to them on the records, you know. It was a really, really nice time, because people were really into the music. Like, people would save up money for weeks to get ready for the dance. They'd be saving for weeks when the bands would come down to play the dance, and they'd be ready, you know, with new outfits and new hairdos and everything. They'd really get ready when the band came to town. Maybe...maybe ... At least 25 percent of them would be standing…
